business: ExceptionOS, supplier-delivery exception intelligence for mid-market manufacturers
target: Purchasing, materials and supply chain people at U.S. discrete / make-to-order manufacturers with 100-500 employees, 3-30 buyers, 100+ suppliers, on a mid-market ERP (Epicor, Infor SyteLine, NetSuite, Dynamics 365/Business Central, Acumatica, Plex)
where: United States (Midwest and Southeast industrial states especially)

segments.name: Purchasing or materials manager (owns the team and the shortage meeting)
Supply chain director or VP (owns OTIF, expedite cost, budget)
COO, GM or owner of a 100-500 person manufacturer

behaviours.name: Spreadsheet owner
behaviours.how: Runs the open-PO / shortage tracker in Excel and trusts it more than the ERP.

behaviours.name: ERP loyalist
behaviours.how: Wants everything inside the ERP and asks the ERP partner first.

behaviours.name: Burned by software
behaviours.how: Lived through a painful ERP or software rollout and is wary of new tools.

behaviours.name: Improvement champion
behaviours.how: Runs lean/continuous-improvement projects and tries new tools if they prove ROI.

behaviours.name: Budget gatekeeper
behaviours.how: Every new spend needs a payback story for the owner or CFO.

behaviours.name: Security-first IT partner
behaviours.how: Won't share ERP or email data with a startup without IT and security sign-off.

objections: Our ERP already flags late POs; we just need discipline
We'd have to give a startup access to our ERP and supplier email
Integration with our ERP will take IT months we don't have
Another tool my buyers have to log into
We tried supplier portals and suppliers ignored them
AI will get a date wrong and we'll miss a shortage
No budget this year unless it pays back fast
A pre-MVP startup might not be around next year
habits: you hold a daily or weekly shortage / expedite meeting
you spend part of every morning in Outlook chasing supplier acknowledgements
you paid for premium freight to cover a late supplier in the last quarter
your plant runs Epicor (or Infor SyteLine) and the ERP partner does customisations
your company grew through an acquisition and runs two ERPs
you report on-time delivery to customers every month
